findings.body: React reconciles these stateful GrafanaRuleListItem/RuleActionsButtons instances by array index, producing key warnings and allowing menu, modal, or drawer state to be retained by a different rule after reordering.
findings.failure_mode: List reconciliation can associate stateful action UI with the wrong rule.
findings.impact: React reconciles these stateful GrafanaRuleListItem/RuleActionsButtons instances by array index, producing key warnings and allowing menu, modal, or drawer state to be retained by a different rule after reordering.
findings.root_cause: The existing key destructured from ruleWithOrigin is not applied to the new GrafanaRuleListItem branch.
findings.suggested_fix: Pass `key={key}` to GrafanaRuleListItem, matching the datasource and unknown-rule branches.
findings.title: Filtered Grafana rule items are rendered without React keys
findings.trigger: Filtered results are replaced or reordered as asynchronous sources/pages complete or the filter changes.
findings.verifier_reason: The patch at FilterView.tsx line 157 shows GrafanaRuleListItem rendered without a key prop, while line 152 destructures `key` from ruleWithOrigin. Lines 165 and 169 show sibling branches (DataSourceRuleLoader, UnknownRuleListItem) correctly pass `key={key}`. This is a concrete React reconciliation bug introduced by the patch - the key exists but is not passed to the component.

pr.title: Alerting: Remove ruler from alert list view2

raw_findings.body: The menu item is displayed based on the new Prometheus ability, but the list item has no rulerRule and RuleActionsButtons only mounts SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer when rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule) is true. Clicking the action therefore changes state without rendering a drawer.
raw_findings.failure_mode: A visible, authorized menu action is a no-op in the alert list.
raw_findings.impact: The menu item is displayed based on the new Prometheus ability, but the list item has no rulerRule and RuleActionsButtons only mounts SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer when rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule) is true. Clicking the action therefore changes state without rendering a drawer.
raw_findings.root_cause: The new ability calculation authorizes silence from promRule while the action implementation still requires a ruler rule.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Allow the silence drawer to be opened from a GrafanaPromRuleDTO (for example, pass its UID to a drawer that does not require a RulerGrafanaRuleDTO), or do not expose the silence item until that path is supported.
raw_findings.title: Silence action cannot open its drawer for Prometheus-only list items
raw_findings.trigger: A user with folder silence permission opens the More menu for a Grafana-managed alerting rule rendered from the Prometheus-only list response and selects Silence notifications.

raw_findings.body: Although canDelete becomes true from the Prometheus rule ability, AlertRuleMenu still renders Delete only under `canDelete && rulerRule`. Since the new list does not supply rulerRule, the authorized user has no delete action.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Users cannot delete Grafana-managed rules from the alert list after ruler fetching is removed.
raw_findings.impact: Although canDelete becomes true from the Prometheus rule ability, AlertRuleMenu still renders Delete only under `canDelete && rulerRule`. Since the new list does not supply rulerRule, the authorized user has no delete action.
raw_findings.root_cause: The permission path was migrated to promRule but the Delete menu rendering retains its rulerRule presence gate.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Render Delete based on canDelete and the editable identifier rather than requiring rulerRule; the existing handleDelete callback already deletes by identifier and group identifier.
raw_findings.title: Delete remains inaccessible for Prometheus-only Grafana rules
raw_findings.trigger: A user with delete permission views a Grafana-managed rule from the new list, which supplies only promRule, and opens its More menu.

raw_findings.body: The new Grafana Prometheus ability reports pause as allowed, but the menu still requires `rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule)` before rendering MenuItemPauseRule. With no ruler rule passed from the list, Pause/Restore disappears.
raw_findings.failure_mode: An available rule-management operation is silently omitted from the list UI.
raw_findings.impact: The new Grafana Prometheus ability reports pause as allowed, but the menu still requires `rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule)` before rendering MenuItemPauseRule. With no ruler rule passed from the list, Pause/Restore disappears.
raw_findings.root_cause: Prometheus-based pause authorization was added without migrating the ruler-dependent pause UI.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Implement the pause control using the Prometheus rule/identifier or retain the ruler data needed by MenuItemPauseRule; otherwise mark pause unsupported in the Prometheus-only ability path.
raw_findings.title: Pause action is authorized but never rendered without a ruler rule
raw_findings.trigger: A user with edit permission opens the More menu for a pausable Grafana-managed alerting rule rendered from the Prometheus-only list response.

raw_findings.body: The new link omits the `returnTo` query value that the removed GrafanaRuleLoader added via createReturnTo, so the details page cannot return the user to their original filtered list context.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Navigation from a list result loses the user's list state.
raw_findings.impact: The new link omits the `returnTo` query value that the removed GrafanaRuleLoader added via createReturnTo, so the details page cannot return the user to their original filtered list context.
raw_findings.root_cause: The replacement list item copied the view URL but dropped the return-location parameter.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Create and pass the same returnTo value used by the removed loader to createRelativeUrl when building the view href.

raw_findings.body: isPluginProvidedRule is the ruler-rule predicate used by the previous implementation, while `rule` here is a GrafanaPromRuleDTO. If its ruler DTO parameter is retained, TypeScript rejects this call and the frontend build cannot complete.
raw_findings.failure_mode: The TypeScript compilation path for alerting abilities fails on the mismatched DTO argument.
raw_findings.impact: isPluginProvidedRule is the ruler-rule predicate used by the previous implementation, while `rule` here is a GrafanaPromRuleDTO. If its ruler DTO parameter is retained, TypeScript rejects this call and the frontend build cannot complete.
raw_findings.root_cause: The new Prometheus-rule ability implementation reuses a ruler-rule-specific helper without adapting its input type.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Add a GrafanaPromRuleDTO-compatible plugin-provenance predicate (or widen and implement isPluginProvidedRule for both DTO shapes) and call that from this hook.
raw_findings.title: Grafana Prometheus abilities pass an incompatible rule DTO to the plugin predicate
raw_findings.trigger: Type-checking the changed useAbilities module after useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities is compiled.

raw_findings.body: The function comment still says that the loader fetches from both Prometheus and Ruler endpoints, but the changed implementation now waits only for and renders the Prometheus response. This misstates the component's data source and can lead to incorrect maintenance assumptions.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Source documentation describes behavior the component no longer performs.

raw_findings.root_cause: The ruler query was removed without updating the adjacent loader documentation.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Update the function comment to state that it loads and polls only the Prometheus endpoint, and remove the obsolete Ruler wording.

The patch context shows both ruler and prom abilities are checked, and the component receives both props. Without concrete evidence that the new list path passes promRule without rulerRule, this is ungrounded speculation about runtime behavior.

validated_findings.body: React reconciles these stateful GrafanaRuleListItem/RuleActionsButtons instances by array index, producing key warnings and allowing menu, modal, or drawer state to be retained by a different rule after reordering.
validated_findings.failure_mode: List reconciliation can associate stateful action UI with the wrong rule.
validated_findings.impact: React reconciles these stateful GrafanaRuleListItem/RuleActionsButtons instances by array index, producing key warnings and allowing menu, modal, or drawer state to be retained by a different rule after reordering.
validated_findings.root_cause: The existing key destructured from ruleWithOrigin is not applied to the new GrafanaRuleListItem branch.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Pass `key={key}` to GrafanaRuleListItem, matching the datasource and unknown-rule branches.
validated_findings.title: Filtered Grafana rule items are rendered without React keys
validated_findings.trigger: Filtered results are replaced or reordered as asynchronous sources/pages complete or the filter changes.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: The patch at FilterView.tsx line 157 shows GrafanaRuleListItem rendered without a key prop, while line 152 destructures `key` from ruleWithOrigin. Lines 165 and 169 show sibling branches (DataSourceRuleLoader, UnknownRuleListItem) correctly pass `key={key}`. This is a concrete React reconciliation bug introduced by the patch - the key exists but is not passed to the component.

validated_findings.verifier_reason: The test at line 207 expects 4 menu items and the candidate claims Delete should be present. However, the test grants AlertingRuleDelete permission (line 49) but the menu rendering at AlertRuleMenu.tsx line 165 requires `canDelete && rulerRule`.
